issue: Simplification: `plan` copies `run`'s pre-walk checks one by one: the engine check with the message repeated word for word at tar_archive.py:87 and :136, the source is_dir/exists branch, the containment check, and `_normalize_items`. That copy is how the two drifts above crept in. Move the checks into one shared validator that returns (status, reason) and call it from both `plan` and `run`.

Simplification: `Runner._plan` (runner.py:54-59) and `_run_instance` (runner.py:82-88) build the same `call_kwargs` dict; only `dry_run` differs. Use one `_call_kwargs(name, instance, now)` helper and add `dry_run` at the call site.
The test builds its expected `reason` by calling `TarArchive().plan(...)`, the code under test, so it can never catch a wrong reason on a `run` row. Assert `""` instead.

The duplicate check compares paths as text only, as the spec says. It misses two names for one file on case-insensitive APFS (`~/Backup/x.tgz` vs `~/backup/x.tgz`) and a relative vs absolute spelling of the same file (`x.tgz` vs `$PWD/x.tgz`). So two instances can still write one archive and race. The docs mention only symlinks as not resolved.
reason: specified lexical normpath behavior; broader file identity is outside PRD scope

issue: `replaces` uses `out.exists()`, which follows symlinks. A dangling symlink at `out` reports `replaces=False` even though `os.replace` will overwrite it. The rest of plan uses `lexists`, so this is inconsistent.
The `_run_plan` docstring still says it only runs and renders steps. It does not mention the `plan_only` branch that prints plan rows and never executes anything.
Unconfirmed whether README.md documents backup CLI flags. The capsule invariant says every CLI change updates README.md, but only backup.rst and CHANGELOG.md were touched.
reason: README lists the tool only; it does not enumerate backup flags; rg inspection refuted missing flag documentation

issue: Known limitation: the plan's item check ignores exclusions. If every present item is excluded, the plan shows `run` but the actual run skips. The PRD specifies a lexists-only check.
